sections.html:
Worcester County's second most populous city, Leominster lies north of Worcester and northwest of Boston. The 2020 census counted 43,782 residents, and the 2024 estimate is 44,209. It covers 29.7 square miles on a plateau above the Nashua River.

The 2020 count was 17,873 households in 18,732 housing units, 4.6 percent of them vacant. With a homeowner vacancy rate of 0.8 percent and a rental rate of 4.1 percent, owned houses seldom sit empty. Route 2 and Route 12 pass through, and Interstate 190, Route 13 and Route 117 begin or end here, and that network pulls shoppers and commuters from far around.

Leominster calls itself the Pioneer Plastics City. Combs came first (146 workers in 24 comb factories by 1853), then celluloid in 1868, then injection molding. Foster Grant sold 20 million pairs of plastic sunglasses in 1937, Tupperware began here in 1938, and the plastic pink flamingo was invented in Leominster in 1956.

The town was incorporated in 1740 and became a city on November 2, 1915. Population jumped from 2,069 in 1840 to 19,744 by 1920 as Irish, French Canadian and Italian workers arrived, and much of the housing dates from that boom. Buyers will ask what has been updated.

Leominster is divided into small villages, and their names still show up in listings.

  • French Hill: a hill of planned triple-decker blocks between 1st and 12th Streets, named for its French immigrant population.
  • Lincoln Terrace: where Italian families settled in the early 1900s.
  • North Leominster: home to the MBTA station on the Fitchburg Line.
  • Morse Hollow, Rice Hill, the Flats, the Bowery, the West Side and the Car Barn area: other named areas.
  • North and South Monoosnoc Hills: high ground in the west, with the South hill at 1,020 feet.

Housing type changes a lot between these areas, so say which one your property is in.

On September 11, 2023, heavy rain caused serious flooding in Leominster and a state of emergency was declared. Monoosnoc Brook runs through the center of the city.

Did water reach your basement or yard that day? Buyers will ask. Hold on to repair invoices, photos and insurance papers so you can explain what was fixed.

A cash buyer can take a house with storm or moisture damage as it stands. We would look at the foundation, the sump and any mold in person, then base an offer on repair costs instead of asking you to restore everything first.

The MBTA Fitchburg Line stops at North Leominster, and the Montachusett Regional Transit Authority runs local buses in Leominster, Fitchburg and Gardner. Retail centers such as Twin City Plaza and the Mall at Whitney Field make the city one of Central Massachusetts' largest shopping destinations, so traffic near them is a fact of life for houses on those roads, and buyers weigh that.

Outdoor space includes the 4,300 acre Leominster State Forest and the 167 acre Doyle Community Park, both worth a mention if your house is close.

This office bills real estate, personal property, water and sewer, and excise. It also issues municipal lien certificates and administers tax titles, liens and foreclosed land sales. It is at City Hall, Room 1, 25 West Street, and the phone is 978-534-7500, extension 1172.

Thursday8:30 am to 5:30 pm

Quarterly-billing communities generally bill on August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. Ask the office how to request a municipal lien certificate for your closing.

Abatement applications go to the Board of Assessors, and the timeline comes from state law. The application is due on or before the first installment due date of the actual bill, generally February 1 where bills are quarterly.

Assessors get three months to answer. After a denial, or silence that counts as one, you have three months to file with the Appellate Tax Board in Boston, and your taxes must stay current throughout.

The value is set as of January 1 before the fiscal year, so use recent sales of similar houses close to that date as evidence.

Closings here run through attorneys, and the deed is recorded with the Worcester County registry. The seller usually pays deed excise at $2 per $500 of consideration, and the registry can give the exact total.

The local fire department issues the certificate of compliance for smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. Phone once a closing date exists. Battery alarms past 10 years have to be swapped for 10-year sealed photoelectric models.

Your attorney will list anything else needed, such as payoff letters and a final tax balance. We can go through that checklist with you when you request an offer.

After you accept an offer, your attorney orders a title search and drafts or reviews the purchase and sale agreement. The search surfaces mortgages, liens and unpaid municipal charges, and each needs a payoff or a release before the deed can be recorded at the Worcester County registry.

You request the municipal lien certificate from the Collector and book the fire department visit. On closing day you sign the deed and settlement papers, your lenders and any back taxes are paid from the proceeds, and the rest goes to you. Without a bank in the middle, the usual snags are old liens and a missed alarm check, so deal with both first.

Bring your most recent tax bill, water and sewer balance, mortgage payoff statement and copies of any leases. For flood or moisture repairs, bring invoices and photos. For an inherited house, bring the documents showing who may sign. A buyer who sees a tidy folder can quote a firmer price and a shorter closing, and your attorney will not have to chase you for a missing page while a closing date hangs in the balance. If something is missing, ask the office that issued it early, because copies can take a few days.

sections.h2: Selling a triple-decker or storm-damaged house
sections.html:
Leominster owners often hold multi-family buildings on French Hill and similar blocks, rental units with tenants in place, or houses with moisture problems. You can sell any of these as they stand. The buyer will want to see each unit, the heating and electrical systems and the basement.

Plan for the fire department certificate, any tax payoff and a lien certificate from the Collector. Collect them before you accept a closing date, and a cash sale can move at the speed of your paperwork rather than a lender's.

faqs.a: Leominster is in Worcester County, Massachusetts, and deeds are recorded through the county registry system.

faqs.q: Who handles tax liens and municipal lien certificates in Leominster?
faqs.a: The Collector and Treasurer's office at City Hall handles tax titles, liens and municipal lien certificates. Call 978-534-7500, extension 1172, during office hours.

faqs.q: Can I sell a French Hill triple-decker in Leominster as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell the building in its current condition. Expect the buyer to review units, tenants and systems, and plan for the fire department certificate and any tax payoff.
Yes. Heavy rain on September 11, 2023 flooded parts of the city and a state of emergency followed. If your house was hit, keep records of every repair.

faqs.q: Is a smoke and CO certificate needed to sell in Leominster?
faqs.a: Yes. The state wants the fire department's compliance certificate on any sale or transfer. Call early and ask about its fee.
